title: Construction Authorization and Choice Improvement Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the House passed version is repeated here.)

Construction Authorization and Choice Improvement Act

(Sec. 2) This bill authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out the replacement of the existing VA Medical Center in Denver, Colorado, in FY2015 in an amount not to exceed $900 million.

(Sec. 3) The 40-mile distance requirement for a veteran to use a non-VA medical facility under the veterans choice program of the Veterans Access, Choice, and Accountability Act of 2014 shall be construed to allow a veteran to access a non-VA medical facility if:

  • the veteran resides more than 40 miles driving distance from the closest VA facility; or
  • the veteran faces an unusual or excessive burden in traveling to such VA medical facility not only because of geographical challenges (as under current law) but also because of environmental factors, such as roads that are not accessible to the general public, traffic, or hazardous weather, because of a medical condition that impacts the ability to travel, or because of other factors as the Secretary determines.

summary.headline: This 2015 law lets the VA spend up to $900 million to replace the Denver VA Medical Center and widens when veterans may use non-VA medical facilities under the veterans choice program.
summary.what_it_does: It authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to replace the existing VA Medical Center in Denver, Colorado, in fiscal year 2015, with spending capped at $900 million. It also changes how the 40-mile distance rule in the veterans choice program is applied. Under the change, a veteran may use a non-VA facility if they live more than 40 driving miles from the closest VA facility, or if traveling to a VA facility is an unusual or excessive burden. That burden can come from geography, road access, traffic, hazardous weather, a medical condition that affects travel, or other factors the Secretary decides.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans in Denver and the surrounding area
who_it_affects.how: They are served by the Denver VA Medical Center, which the law authorizes the VA to replace.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who live more than 40 driving miles from a VA facility
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to get care at a non-VA medical facility under the veterans choice program.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans facing travel burdens such as poor road access, hazardous weather, or medical conditions that make travel hard
who_it_affects.how: They may qualify to use a non-VA facility even if they live within 40 miles of a VA facility.
It is authorized to spend up to $900 million on the Denver facility and to apply the expanded travel-burden standard when deciding whether veterans may use non-VA care.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a separate effective date for these provisions. The law was enacted on May 22, 2015, and the Denver authorization refers to fiscal year 2015.
